problems.comment:
Up to 15 cm of snow has fallen since Monday above approximately 2400 m. 10 to 15 cm of snow will fall until Friday. The new snow and wind slabs are lying on top of a weakly bonded old snowpack in particular on shady slopes above approximately 2400 m. In some places avalanches can be triggered in the old snow. Mostly they are small. 
 Backcountry touring calls for careful route selection. The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

bulletin.snowpack:
Snow cover
Since Monday, there have been repeated episodes of light snow at high altitude, accompanied by a moderate southwesterly wind. Snow will continue to fall in the north until Friday morning, sometimes down to low altitudes towards the end of the precipitation.
The fresh snow is primarily lying on shady slopes above approximately 2400 m on a thin old snow cover that has mostly undergone faceting. Fractures are therefore to be expected in the old snowpack, especially where a continuous, widespread snow cover was already present before this week's snowfall.
Isolated wet slides of fresh snow are possible on sunny slopes.
bulletin.tendency:
Outlook
Saturday
Conditions will be mostly sunny in the north, with sunny intervals in the south. There will be scarcely any change in avalanche danger on shady slopes. Human activity may trigger avalanches, especially on shady slopes in the high Alpine regions.
Sunday
A little snow will fall above 1800 m over the course of the day in the west. Conditions will be mostly sunny in the east and cloudy in the south. There will be scarcely any change in the danger of dry avalanches.
